description: Can I reach the internet? Can the internet reach me? Why is my app slow? Who is using all the bandwidth?

panels.description: Endpoints that can’t be reached right now. Zero is healthy. If this is non-zero, check the table below to see which probe failed and why.
panels.title: Probes Failing

panels.description: Days until the soonest-expiring TLS certificate among all monitored HTTPS probes (9 certs currently tracked: auth, cleanuparr, grafana, prowlarr, qbit, radarr, sonarr, uptime, whoami). See the TLS Certificates table below for the full per-domain breakdown.
panels.title: Nearest Cert Expiry

panels.description: Average probe success rate over the dashboard time range. 100% = every probe passed every check. Drops below 100% indicate intermittent connectivity issues even if everything is passing right now.
panels.title: Probe Uptime

panels.description: All connectivity checks. Failures sort first. If internet fails but dns passes → routing/firewall issue. If both fail → total internet outage. Click a probe name to check its logs.
panels.title: Probe Status

panels.description: ICMP reachability of the LAN gateway/router (192.168.1.1) from the monitoring VM. If this fails while NAS/Internet still pass, the router itself is the suspect -- the prime candidate for WAN-edge issues like remote Plex buffering. If this passes but Internet fails, the problem is beyond the router (ISP/modem).
panels.title: Router (LAN Gateway)

panels.description: ICMP reachability of the Synology NAS from the monitoring VM. Compare against Router/Internet to isolate a local-network issue from a WAN issue.
panels.title: NAS

panels.description: ICMP reachability of an external host (1.1.1.1), confirming the WAN path beyond the router is up. If Router passes but this fails, the problem is upstream of the router (ISP or modem) -- not this network.
panels.title: Internet (WAN)

panels.description: Round-trip ICMP latency for the three LAN/WAN reference points side by side. Router should be sub-millisecond to a few ms; if router latency spikes while NAS/Internet stay flat, suspect the router itself. If all three spike together, suspect the monitoring VM or its host.
panels.title: ICMP Latency: Router vs NAS vs Internet

panels.description: Total round-trip time per probe over time. Rising latency often precedes outages. Compare internal probes (grafana, core-dnsmasq, nas) against the external reference probes (internet, dns — both target 1.1.1.1) to isolate whether slowness is inside your network or outside. Probes are defined by BLACKBOX_*_TARGETS in .env; every configured probe appears here automatically.
panels.title: Response Latency

panels.description: Breaks HTTP probe time into phases for the probe(s) selected in $probe (defaults to All, which averages across every HTTP probe — narrow to one probe to see its own breakdown without dilution). If resolve is high → DNS problem. If tls is high → cert/handshake issue. If processing is high → the app itself is slow. If transfer is high → response is large or network is congested.
panels.title: Where Is the Latency?

panels.description: Green = reachable, red = unreachable. If all probes go red simultaneously → total internet outage. If only one goes red → that specific service is down. Gaps indicate Prometheus scrape misses.
panels.title: Uptime History

panels.description: Total network traffic (rx+tx) per container, stacked. This includes both internal (container-to-container) and external (internet) traffic — cAdvisor cannot distinguish them. For media/VPN stacks, the VPN container (ExpressVPN) traffic is a good proxy for actual internet egress. To measure true internet-only bandwidth, add node_exporter to the host and monitor the physical NIC.

targets.expr: sum by (service) (rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Container Traffic

panels.description: Containers ranked by current combined network traffic. Includes internal + external. In a VPN media stack, the vpn container’s traffic represents actual internet usage. Click to investigate.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (host, service) (rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Top Traffic

panels.description: Real physical NIC throughput (rx+tx) per VM's eth0 interface, from node_exporter. Unlike Container Traffic above (cAdvisor rx+tx, which mixes internal container-to-container traffic with real external traffic -- a known, documented limitation), this is the actual wire-level rate for each VM's uplink.

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{device="eth0", node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{device="eth0", node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Physical NIC Throughput (per VM, rx+tx)

panels.description: Packet errors and drops per VM's eth0 interface, from node_exporter. Errors should be zero. A small constant drop rate (a few packets/sec) on every VM is common background noise on a shared Proxmox bridge (broadcast/multicast frames the guest doesn't consume) -- shown yellow, not red. Sustained high rates (tens+ per second) indicate a real driver/hardware/congestion problem -- shown red.
panels.title: Packet Errors & Drops (per VM)

panels.description: Whether the ExpressVPN tunnel is connected. Green = tunnel up, Red = disconnected. If disconnected, qBittorrent traffic is blocked by Network Lock.
panels.title: VPN Status

panels.description: State of the ExpressVPN tunnel over time. expressvpn_connection_uptime_seconds is permanently 0 on the current Lightway/WireGuard tunnel (the exporter can't read uptime for that tunnel type), and expressvpn_last_state_change_timestamp_seconds was verified to re-stamp on every scrape rather than only on real state changes -- neither can drive a trustworthy uptime stat. This timeline uses expressvpn_connection_status directly instead: solid green means connected for the entire window shown; any red means the tunnel dropped.
panels.title: VPN Connection State

panels.description: Number of VPN connection failures during the dashboard time range. Zero is healthy. Non-zero indicates the VPN had trouble connecting — check ExpressVPN container logs for details.
panels.title: Connect Failures

panels.description: Traffic through the vpn container's network namespace, as reported by cAdvisor. qBittorrent shares this namespace (network_mode: service:vpn), so this is effectively torrent traffic plus WebUI/scrape chatter. The ExpressVPN exporter's own interface counters (expressvpn_network_rx_bytes_total, tx_bytes_total, etc.) are live and reporting real data on the current tunnel -- see the TX Drops stat alongside this panel, sourced directly from the exporter.
panels.title: VPN Traffic

panels.description: Transmit-side packet drop rate reported directly by the ExpressVPN exporter (expressvpn_network_tx_dropped_total). This counter is naturally bursty under real download load (observed 0-45 pkt/s over the past week, not a flat baseline) -- thresholds are calibrated against that range, not against "any nonzero = bad". Unaffected by the broken uptime metric above.
panels.title: VPN TX Drop Rate

panels.description: Days until expiry for every TLS certificate Blackbox is currently monitoring, one row per probe. Sorted soonest-first.
panels.title: Certificate Expiry (All Probes)
